extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of rhetoric/composition (writers, teachers of style, classical rhetoricians)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing plain (and contrasted elevated) prose: rules for diction, sentence structure, clarity, vividness, persuasive effect, and epistolary style drawn from classical rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use current and familiar diction (plain style)
rubrics_metrics.description: The diction throughout should be current and familiar; the more familiar an expression is the homelier it is, while the unusual and metaphorical is elevated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid compound words, newly-coined words, or any other words which contribute to elevation. Above all, the style should be lucid. (Original phrasing: 'The diction throughout should be current and familiar... Compound words should—not_be_admitted ... nor yet newly-coined words ... Above all, the style should be lucid.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer bound, connected phrasing (lucidity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lucidity involves employment of current words, and next, of words bound together; writing which is wholly disjointed and unconnected is entirely lacking in clearness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conjunctions to compact and consolidate members so the reader can discern beginnings of members; loose/disjointed structure (as in Heracleitus) causes obscurity. The compacted style is 'pleasant to read' and better for the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broken/disjointed (histrionic) style for acting/debate
rubrics_metrics.description: The disjointed style lends itself better to debate and bears the name 'histrionic,' since a broken structure stimulates acting and delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short, broken members to force dramatic delivery (example: 'Thee I received, I bare, I nurse, O dear one.' vs. the lifeless 'I received and bare and nurse'). Reserve this style for stage/actorical contexts rather than literary reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid affectation and unnecessary inversions
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid affected inversions, unnatural rhythms, and other signs of affectation which elevate or make style effeminate or undignified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affected rhythms and inversions (e.g., Sotadean inversions) produce an undignified, effeminate gait; keep order and diction natural unless elevation is intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow natural word order; begin with nominative in narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural order of the words should be followed; in narrative passages we should begin with the nominative case (subject) or with the accusative for certain styles but avoid dependent cases which cause obscurity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Epidamnus is a town...' is clearer. Reversals ('There is a town Ephyra') are permissible but not preferred for clarity. Avoid putting dependent cases at the beginning which keep readers 'on the rack of grammatical uncertainty.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use repetition (epanalepsis) to aid clearness and emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Epanalepsis' is the repetition of the same particle in the course of a lengthy sentence; repetition of the same word can remind and set the prelude again, aiding clearness and vividness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: repeating 'indeed' or repeating a phrase ('to his discredit... now that he is dead write to his discredit') increases vividness and emphasis. But avoid useless repetition that merely wastes words—use it where it enhances clarity or effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive terseness and hurried sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive terseness may give pleasure but fails in clearness: hurried movement of a sentence may make its meaning imperfectly caught.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer slightly longer, clearer constructions when necessary; rephrase complex constructions into straightforward ones (example transforming complex accusative constructions into explicit nominative + verb clauses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep amplifications and long members within due bounds (plain style)
rubrics_metrics.description: An attempt must be made to keep amplifications within due bounds; long members tend to elevation and should be avoided in the plain style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break off clauses to give pauses; prefer trimeter-like short members and frequent rests in plain prose. Long, rambling sentences increase elevation and reduce plain-style clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: End members with precision; avoid prolonged endings in plain style
rubrics_metrics.description: In the plain style the members should end with precision and rest on a sure foundation; prolonged endings belong rather to the elevated style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft sentence endings to be concise and secure; avoid the 'prolonged endings' typical of elevated, heroic diction (e.g., Thucydides' long appositions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid concurrence of long vowel-sounds and diphthongs in plain style
rubrics_metrics.description: In the plain style we must shun the concurrence of long vowel-sounds and of diphthongs, since lengthening invariably suggests elaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If concurrence occurs prefer short vowels or mixes of short+long; this keeps the plain style unimpressive and every-day rather than ornate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid peculiar figures and eccentricity in plain style
rubrics_metrics.description: Peculiar figures should be avoided, since all eccentricity is unfamiliar and extraordinary and thus elevates the style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain style welcomes vivid representation and persuasiveness but not striking figures; use ordinary expression unless a special effect is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vividness: exact narration and complete detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Vividness arises from an exact narration overlooking no detail and cutting out nothing; mention all things that happen to produce vivid description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Homeric similes and the Patroclus horse-race—narrate accompanying circumstances, sensory detail, and do not omit usual details. Repetition and gradual unfolding (delay revealing a calamity) increase suspense and vividness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vividness techniques: repetition, gradual disclosure, accompaniment, sound
rubrics_metrics.description: Repetition often gives the effect of vividness more than a single statement; unfolding misfortune gradually and mentioning accompanying circumstances increase vividness; onomatopoeia and cacophony can also produce vivid effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include repeated phrasing ('I saved you... you were saved through me'), the messenger slowly revealing Cyrus's death, Homeric onomatopoeic participles like 'lapping', and cacophonous lines to suggest rough ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convincing (persuasive) prose requires lucidity and naturalness
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of convincing depends on two things: lucidity and naturalness. What is not lucid nor natural is not convincing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid exuberant, inflated, or artificial language; composition must be steady-going and void of formal rhythm. Let some points be left unsaid to permit the hearer to infer and become a 'friendly witness' (Theophrastus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Epistolary style: plain but more studied than dialogue; show character; avoid breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter ought to be written in the same manner as a dialogue yet be a little more studied since it is committed to writing; frequent breaks and imitative extemporary turns are less appropriate in letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid imitating conversational brokenness and theatricalities; letters should contain glimpses of character, be adequately crafted in length, and not try to mimic an actor's delivery or debate speech patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dependent constructions (accusatives) that obscure meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of dependent cases and constructions must be avoided, since this leads to obscurity (as in Philistus's style).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewrite sentences with straightforward constructions (e.g., make subject and verb explicit rather than burying them in accusative or dependent clauses) to ensure immediate comprehension.
